title: add interactive browser RAG walkthrough using Web Worker + offline index
author: Priya Sinha
release_notes: Introduce a browser-focused RAG quickstart demonstrating an offline index and Web Worker-based embedder; no breaking API changes.
body:
Motivation: provide a lightweight, self-contained browser quickstart that demonstrates a minimal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) flow without requiring a backend. Many customers prototype knowledge features in the browser and run into pitfalls around blocking main-thread embedding computation and large synchronous index loads. This PR adds a walkthrough and an opinionated example that uses a Web Worker to compute embeddings, a tiny on-disk JSONL index (vector_index.jsonl) for demo corpora, and the Redwood SDK client in a restricted browser environment.

What changed (high level): the PR adds a step-by-step guide (docs/guides/browser-rag-webworker-quickstart.md), a runnable example (examples/browser-rag/) with a minimal HTML UI, a Web Worker implementation for async embedding generation (worker/embeddings_worker.ts compiled to embeddings_worker.js), a small sample vector index (worker/vector_index.jsonl) and a telemetry snippet to show how to capture latency and token usage from the browser. The example intentionally relies on in-browser approximate nearest neighbor search (brute-force L2 for the small demo index) and documents how to replace it with a WASM ANN library for larger corpora.

Checklist: - [x] Guide with prerequisites and security considerations (CORS, CSP, local file sizes). - [x] Example project with step-by-step run instructions. - [x] Web Worker-based embedder and graceful fallback to remote embedding API. - [x] Telemetry example that reports token/latency metrics to a configured endpoint (opt-in). - [x] Docs site navigation entry. - [x] Smoke tested on Chrome (desktop) and Firefox.

How to run locally (short): 1) cd examples/browser-rag 2) npm ci && npm run build 3) npx http-server -c-1 ./ (or open index.html via local dev server) 4) Open Developer Tools -> Network and Console. The README has troubleshooting hints for CSP and local file sizes.

Testing and QA notes: small automated smoke job added to the docs pipeline triggers a static render and link-check. A manual preview was created in our docs preview environment to validate images and the interactive UI. We exercised the fallback path where the Web Worker cannot compute embeddings (Safari private mode) and verified the UI surfaces the remote-embed option.

Security note: the example ships a tiny sample index and documents that production datasets should never be embedded client-side. The telemetry snippet is opt-in and respects a user toggle; no secrets are embedded in the example.

Related: links to ENG-1947 (internal spec), DOCS-332 (content plan). This is intentionally self-contained so customers can fork the example and swap the index for a backend call or a WASM ANN library.

Merge: squash-merged after reviewers approved and CI green.

review_comments: Ethan Cole (request changes): The worker fallback path should be more explicit in the guide; unclear what happens on Safari iOS. Please add a short note and a test scenario.
Priya Sinha (author reply): Added Safari notes and a documented fallback test (see README steps). The worker now returns a structured error that the UI surfaces to the user.
Marta Ruiz (suggestion): Telemetry opt-in toggle looks good; can we add a one-line example showing how to attach a Datadog/OTLP endpoint?
Priya Sinha (author reply): Added telemetry-config.yaml and a short paragraph that shows how to wire OTLP collectors; the example keeps defaults off.
Jun Park (approved): Verified example builds and smoke tests pass in preview. UX of the policy/csp doc looks clear. Approving.

notes: This PR is deliberately conservative: small demo index, clear security guidance, and a documented path to move embeddings/server-side for production workloads. Follow-on work tracked in ENG-1947 will include WASM ANN integration and a larger on-disk demo index.
